title: CX-MT044-ApprovalConsentBridge
clause: Bridge item/commandExecution|fileChange requestApproval into ConsentGate; deny-by-default timeout; per-session approval policy; ledgered decisions+latencies

scope.summary:
GOAL: Bridge Codex app-server server-to-client approval requests (item/commandExecution/requestApproval and item/fileChange/requestApproval) into Handshake's consent machinery: the existing ConsentGate (model_runtime/cloud/consent_gate.rs) with the cloud escalation policy applied, per-session approval policy configuration (auto-approve classes vs operator-gated), deny-by-default on gate timeout, and a decision + latency ledger for every request.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New file src/backend/handshake_core/src/model_runtime/cloud/codex_app_server/approvals.rs implementing CodexApprovalBridge, registered as the MT-041 server-request handler for the two approval methods; a typed per-session ApprovalPolicy config; unit tests. Re-export additions in codex_app_server/mod.rs. ConsentGate itself is consumed, not modified (any genuinely required extension is an HBR-STOP-005 disclosure, not a silent edit).

DETAILED SPEC:
1. SERVER-REQUEST HANDLING. The app-server sends JSON-RPC REQUESTS (with id) to the client when the running agent wants to execute a command (item/commandExecution/requestApproval) or apply a file change (item/fileChange/requestApproval). MT-041 routes server-requests to a registered handler; this MT registers CodexApprovalBridge for exactly these two methods. The bridge MUST respond to every request id exactly once with the schema-defined approve/deny response shape (taken from `codex app-server generate-json-schema` at implementation time); an unanswered approval id wedges the agent's turn.
2. REQUEST TYPING. Parse each request into a typed ApprovalRequest: kind (CommandExecution{command, cwd, ...schema fields} | FileChange{changes summary, paths, ...schema fields}), thread_id, turn_id, item_id, received_at. Unknown extra fields are preserved raw for the ledger.
3. POLICY EVALUATION. A typed per-session ApprovalPolicy is attached at thread start (MT-042 session context): { auto_approve_classes: [ApprovalClass], operator_gated: default }. ApprovalClass examples: ReadOnlyCommand (classification conservative: only commands matching a vetted read-only allowlist), FileChangeWithinSessionWorktree (every touched path canonicalizes inside the pinned session worktree), Any (explicit opt-in, off by default). Evaluation order: (a) if the request matches an auto-approve class -> approve WITHOUT operator round-trip, ledger records auto_approved+class; (b) otherwise -> operator-gated path via ConsentGate.
4. CONSENTGATE BRIDGE. Operator-gated requests call ConsentGate::check_or_prompt (consent_gate.rs line 85) with session_id + a lane identifier for the codex app-server lane; the gate's ConsentProvider prompts the operator (or applies remembered consent). The cloud escalation policy applies: escalation/prompt routing follows the same policy surface the cloud lanes use (cloud/mod.rs wires the gate into cloud runtimes, lines 18-24). ConsentDecision::Approved -> approve response; ConsentDecision::Denied / ConsentGateError -> deny response (typed reason in ledger).
5. DENY-BY-DEFAULT TIMEOUT. The gate consultation runs under a bounded deadline (default 120s, per-session configurable). On timeout: respond DENY to the app-server (never leave the id hanging, never approve on timeout), ledger records timed_out_denied with the elapsed latency. A denied command/file-change surfaces to the turn as the agent's denied-approval item; the turn continues per app-server semantics (the agent decides its next step) - the bridge never interrupts the turn itself.
6. LEDGER. Every ApprovalRequest produces exactly one ledger record: {request ids (thread/turn/item), kind, policy_path (auto_approved{class} | operator_approved | operator_denied | timed_out_denied | error_denied), decision latency_ms, decided_at}. Records are emitted as FR business events through the lane observability seam (final kind naming per MT-161 lands in MT-045; this MT emits through the seam MT-045 finalizes) and are queryable per session for the annotation/parity surfaces of this WP.
7. FAIL-CLOSED INVARIANTS. Malformed approval request -> deny + typed parse-error ledger record. Handler panic is impossible-by-construction (no unwrap on request fields); any internal error -> deny (error_denied). Two requests with the same id -> second is answered with a typed JSON-RPC error, first decision stands.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read consent_gate.rs fully (ConsentGate line 64, check_or_prompt line 85, ConsentDecision line 42, ConsentProvider line 56, remembered-consent + forget/drop_session semantics lines 134-160) and the cloud gate wiring in cloud/mod.rs (lines 18-24, re-export line 59); read the MT-041 server-request handler contract.
2. Author approvals.rs: ApprovalRequest/ApprovalClass/ApprovalPolicy/ApprovalLedgerRecord types with serde round-trip tests.
3. Implement request parsing with raw-preserving unknown-field capture; malformed -> deny path.
4. Implement policy evaluation (auto-approve classes; conservative ReadOnlyCommand allowlist; worktree-containment check via canonicalized paths against the MT-042 pinned cwd).
5. Implement the ConsentGate consultation with deadline + deny-by-default; map all ConsentGateError variants to deny with typed reasons.
6. Implement the ledger emission and per-session query surface.
7. Register the bridge with the MT-041 client for the two methods; ensure exactly-once response per id.
8. Unit-test against the MT-041 fake transport: auto-approve class hit, operator approve, operator deny, timeout-deny, malformed-deny, duplicate-id, worktree-escape file change (path outside pinned cwd -> NOT auto-approvable), and ledger exhaustiveness (every request has exactly one record).
9. Run proof targets; record outputs.
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/** (no GUI work in this MT)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/model_runtime/cloud/consent_gate.rs (consume; any required extension is an HBR-STOP-005 disclosure)
acceptance_criteria: CodexApprovalBridge is registered for item/commandExecution/requestApproval and item/fileChange/requestApproval and answers EVERY request id exactly once (test incl. duplicate-id case).

Auto-approve classes work: a vetted read-only command and a file change fully inside the pinned session worktree are approved without a gate round-trip, ledgered as auto_approved with the class (tests).
A file change touching any path outside the pinned session worktree is NEVER auto-approved regardless of policy (negative test with canonicalization traversal attempt, e.g. ..\ segments).

Operator-gated path drives ConsentGate::check_or_prompt with session_id + codex lane id; Approved -> approve, Denied -> deny, all ConsentGateError variants -> deny with typed reason (tests using a scripted ConsentProvider).
Gate timeout denies: a ConsentProvider that never answers within the deadline yields a DENY response to the server and a timed_out_denied ledger record with measured latency (test).
Malformed approval request -> deny + parse-error ledger record; no panic (test).
Ledger exhaustiveness: N requests produce exactly N records, each with one of the five policy_path values and a latency_ms (test).
Approval decisions and latencies are emitted as FR business events through the lane observability seam (test asserts emission).
Per-session ApprovalPolicy is attached at thread start and two concurrent sessions with different policies do not cross-contaminate (test).
proof_targets: HSK_CODEX_LIVE=1 cargo test -p handshake_core codex_approval_request_live -- --nocapture --ignored  # live: provoke a real approval request (sandboxed command) and answer deny; absent CLI/login => typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF, never silent skip

implementation_notes: Approve/deny response field shapes MUST come from `codex app-server generate-json-schema` (MT-041 records the authored-against version); do not guess enum casing.
ReadOnlyCommand classification must be allowlist-based (e.g. exact argv0 + flag patterns), never denylist-based; when in doubt the class does not match and the request goes to the operator.
Worktree containment: canonicalize each touched path and require it starts with the canonicalized pinned cwd; symlink escapes fail containment (test on Windows junction if practical, else document).

The sandbox flags of the exec lane (--sandbox workspace-write | danger-full-access) are a DIFFERENT enforcement layer on a different lane; do not treat approval bridging as a sandbox substitute - note this in module docs.
Consent memory semantics (remembered approve per session+lane) come from ConsentGate; do not build a second cache in the bridge.
Timeout deny is deliberately non-configurable to approve-on-timeout; no policy value may invert fail-closed.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless backend bridge MT: the operator prompt surface is the existing ConsentProvider wiring; no new GUI is created here. Visual verification = TraceProjection per HBR-VIS-004.

target_entries: Codex lane: approval requests (what triggers command/file-change approvals, auto-approve classes, operator-gated flow, deny-by-default timeout)
Codex lane: approval ledger (where decisions + latencies are recorded and how to read them per session)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Every approval decision + latency is an FR business event through the lane observability seam (final kinds per MT-161 in MT-045).
Recorded DEFERRED-with-reason if internal_diagnostics is not present in the implementation worktree at claim time; never silently skipped.
Approval-path liveness rides the MT-041 health probe + MT-005 supervisor; external-watcher registration deferred there; recorded, never silently skipped.

risk_if_missed: Agent-requested commands/file-changes either wedge (unanswered approval ids) or bypass Handshake consent entirely; no audit trail of what the operator approved, breaking the WP's steering/consent story and any compliance-grade replay.

risks: RISK-1: Approve-on-timeout inversion - a timeout path that approves (or a config that can flip it) silently executes unreviewed commands.
RISK-2: Auto-approve class over-match - a loose ReadOnlyCommand or containment check auto-approves destructive commands or out-of-worktree writes.
RISK-3: Unanswered approval id - a dropped/paniced handler leaves the agent turn wedged forever with no operator-visible cause.
RISK-4: Ledger gaps - decisions without records (or records without decisions) make the approval trail untrustworthy for audit/replay.
RISK-5: Cross-session policy bleed - one session's permissive auto-approve classes applied to another session's requests.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Deny-by-default hardcoded on timeout and on every error path; no policy field can invert it; tests for timeout and all error variants.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Allowlist-only read-only classification + canonicalized worktree containment with traversal negative tests.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Exactly-once response invariant with duplicate-id test; panic-free parsing (no unwrap); malformed -> deny test.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Ledger exhaustiveness test (N requests == N records) + FR emission assertion.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Policy stored per session context; concurrent two-session isolation test (HBR-SWARM-001).
